Words without brackets are required, `[ ]` marks optional parts, `a | b` alternatives, `...` a repeatable argument and `[,...]` a comma separated list.

## Description

Adds resources to the configuration and exports them. Onesimus extensions read, update and delete resources of the editable types (client, job, jobdefs, schedule, fileset); every change is checked like a reload and written to the configuration directory.

## Subcommands

### configure add {#sub-configure-add}

**Add a resource.**

Creates a new resource of the given type (client, jobdefs, job, storage, catalog, schedule, fileset, pool, messages, counter, profile, console, user). The resource is written to bareos-dir.d/&lt;type&gt;/&lt;name&gt;.conf and loaded into the running Director at once, without reload. Directives are written in lower case without blanks (maximumvolumejobs=1); a directive may repeat where the resource allows it (run= of a schedule). The characters @ and ; are not allowed in values.

The configuration must be in directory form and the directory of the type must already exist. Adding a client also exports its file daemon resource, like configure export. Onesimus deviation: profile and user are always refused (edit them in the configuration files), and console is only accepted as name, password, one or more profile and an optional description, with profiles that grant no more than the creating console may use itself.

```text
configure add client name=<name> [description=<description>]
                     [protocol=<Native|NDMPV2|NDMPV3|NDMPV4>]
                     [authtype=<None|Clear|MD5>] address=<address>
                     [lanaddress=<lanaddress>] [port=<port>]
                     [username=<username>] password=<password>
                     [catalog=<catalog>] [passive=<yes|no>]
                     [connectionfromdirectortoclient=<yes|no>]
                     [connectionfromclienttodirector=<yes|no>]
                     [enabled=<yes|no>] [hardquota=<hardquota>]
                     [softquota=<softquota>]
```

A new backup pool with one job per volume:

```text
configure add pool name=Weekly pooltype=Backup maximumvolumejobs=1 labelformat=Weekly-
```

A schedule with two run lines:

```text
configure add schedule name=Nightly run="Full 1st sun at 23:05" run="Incremental mon-sat at 23:05"
```

A job whose required directives come from a jobdefs:

```text
configure add job name=BackupClient2 jobdefs=DefaultJob client=bareos-fd
```

### configure export {#sub-configure-export}

**Export a client resource.**

Writes the Director resource a file daemon needs to accept this Director, for the given client, to bareos-dir-export/client/&lt;client&gt;/bareos-fd.d/director/. Copy the file to the client into bareos-fd.d/director/. Calling it again overwrites the file with the same content. client= must name a configured client.

```text
configure export client=<client>
```

| Argument | Type | Values / source | Default | Flags | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `client=` | resource | from [`.clients`](../dot-clients/) |  | required | Client name. |

Export the director resource for bareos-fd:

```text
configure export client=bareos-fd
```

### configure read {#sub-configure-read}

<span class="origin-badge origin-badge--onesimus">Onesimus extension</span>

**Show a resource (Onesimus).**

Aliases: `show`, `get`

Onesimus extension: shows a short summary of one client, job, pool or storage of the running configuration (for a client name, address, port and enabled; for a job type, level, client, storage, pool, fileset, priority and enabled). The resource ACLs of the console apply as with show; a resource the console may not see reads like an unknown one. For the raw resource text use .config read.

```text
configure read [client=<client> | job=<job> | pool=<pool> | storage=<storage>]
```

| Argument | Type | Values / source | Default | Flags | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `client=` | resource | from [`.clients`](../dot-clients/) |  | one of: what | Client name. |
| `job=` | resource | from [`.jobs`](../dot-jobs/) |  | one of: what | Job name. |
| `pool=` | resource | from [`.pools`](../dot-pools/) |  | one of: what | Pool name. |
| `storage=` | resource | from [`.storages`](../dot-storage/) |  | one of: what | Storage name. |

Summary of a client:

```text
configure read client=bareos-fd
```

Summary of a job:

```text
configure read job=BackupClient1
```

### configure update {#sub-configure-update}

<span class="origin-badge origin-badge--onesimus">Onesimus extension</span>

**Change directives of a resource (Onesimus).**

Onesimus extension: changes directives of an existing client, job, jobdefs, schedule or fileset in its configuration file and reloads. Only the named directives change; comments, order, indentation and all other directives stay byte for byte. It is checked like odir -t, written atomically, and a failed reload restores the old state. pool, storage and console are refused, as are directives in nested blocks (RunScript, Include, Options) and changing the name.

A directive given several times replaces all its lines (the run lines of a schedule); a directive with an empty value (description=) removes it. A missing directive is added before the closing brace. The resource ACL of the console applies. The old job keys newclient, newstorage and newpool are accepted as client, storage and pool.

| `newpool=` | resource | from [`.pools`](../dot-pools/) |  | repeatable | Directive (empty value removes it). |
| `newstorage=` | resource | from [`.storages`](../dot-storage/) |  | repeatable | Directive (empty value removes it). |
| `newschedule=` | resource | from [`.schedule`](../dot-schedule/) |  | repeatable | Directive (empty value removes it). |

Also accepts the arguments of [configure update](#sub-configure-update): `yes`.

```text
                        [run=<run> ...] [enabled=<yes|no> ...]
```

| `run=` | string |  |  | repeatable | Directive (empty value removes it). |
| `enabled=` | bool | `yes`, `no` |  | repeatable | Directive (empty value removes it). |

Also accepts the arguments of [configure update](#sub-configure-update): `yes`.

### configure delete {#sub-configure-delete}

<span class="origin-badge origin-badge--onesimus">Onesimus extension</span>

**Delete an unreferenced resource (Onesimus).**

Onesimus extension: deletes a client, job, jobdefs, schedule or fileset through the configuration CRUD, the same path as .config delete. The resource is read for its current checksum and deleted only if no other resource still refers to it; otherwise the referring resources are listed and nothing is deleted. The remaining configuration is checked like odir -t, the file change is atomic and a failed reload is rolled back.

pool, storage and console are refused; remove such files by hand and reload. The resource ACL of the console applies.

```text
configure delete client=<client>
configure delete job=<job>
configure delete jobdefs=<jobdefs>
configure delete schedule=<schedule>
configure delete fileset=<fileset>
```

Delete a fileset no job uses any more:

```text
configure delete fileset=OldFileSet
```

Delete a client, refused while a job still names it:

```text
configure delete client=old-fd
```

## Examples

Add a client:

```text
configure add client name=fd2 address=fd2.example.org password=secret
```

A console with the rights of a profile:

```text
configure add console name=ops password=pw profile=operator
```

Replace the Run lines (Onesimus):

```text
configure update schedule=Nightly run="Full sun at 23:00" run="Incremental mon-sat at 23:00"
```

Write the director resource for the file daemon of bareos-fd:

```text
configure export client=bareos-fd
```

Remove an unused schedule (Onesimus):

```text
configure delete schedule=OldNightly
```
